title: Family hopes police learn lesson from shooting probe
article: Dolores Young believes she'll never know the full story of why an RCMP officer shot and killed her unarmed son while his hands were up and he was at least five metres away.
But she has hope other lives will be saved by an investigation announced Wednesday.

"What I hope for is that the police are not so willing to shoot to kill," Young said after learning the Commission for Public Complaints Against the RCMP will investigate the shooting death of 29-year-old Kevin St. Arnaud.

In a statement, commission chairman Paul Kennedy said he would be investigating on the grounds that RCMP officers "improperly entered into a situation with St. Arnaud," and that "a member of the RCMP improperly discharged his firearm in the incident."
Police say they were pursuing St. Arnaud as a robbery suspect in the central B.C. town of Vanderhoof in December 2004.
Const. Ryan Sheremetta claimed when St. Arnaud turned on him in a snowy field and refused to stop, he shot the man three times in the chest.
The regional Crown counsel announced in February that criminal charges would not be laid against Sheremetta.
The commission's investigation was launched after a complaint by the B.C. Civil Liberties Association.
Jason Gratl, president of the association, said the St. Arnaud investigation is a good beginning, but there are three other outstanding deaths that also need to be addressed.
Ian Bush was shot by a Houston police officer in what police say was a struggle while he was being released from custody last October.
Bush, 22, had been arrested for having an open beer at a hockey game but it wasn't until months later that his family found out he had been shot in the back of the head.
A coroner's inquest is being held into Bush's death and a police report is being completed.
Gurmeet Sandhu of Surrey died while being Tasered by an officer in June 2005, and Ryan Snopek died in custody in Cranbrook in January 2005.
Gratl's association will renew its call for inquiries into the other three deaths, which he said cry out for investigations.
"When a man gets shot in the back of the head, you would think the commissioner for complaints against the RCMP would want to get involved," he said, referring to Bush's death.
Cameron Ward, the lawyer for St. Arnaud's common-law wife, said she feels the investigation is a positive development because the circumstances around the death need an independent investigation.
"It is much more independent that having one of the RCMP members investigate one of their own."
